**A.** Under the majority (lien theory) view, a mortgage by one joint tenant only creates a lien on that tenant's interest and doesn't sever the joint tenancy, because title stays with the borrower. The team note has this backwards: that's the title-theory result, not the lien-theory one. When he dies, her survivorship right gives her the whole property, and the bank's lien ends along with his interest, so it can't foreclose.

CONFIDENCE: 88
